_what: A Quiet Pint, a pub under the street, in homage to McAnally's in Jim Butcher's Dresden Files. Ryan Boren's brief, 2026-10-05: a new room on the street, made like McAnally's Pub, with the passages from Storm Front, Proven Guilty, Small Favor and Cold Days that describe it. tools/make-a-quiet-pint.py builds the room, the plan, your table, the board and the credits from this file and refuses what it says it refuses.
_light: The only light in the pub is the street's. It comes in at the top of the walls through the windows, which are at the level of the pavement, and most of it reaches the tables by way of the mirrors, each hung at its own height and tipped its own way, so it lands in patches, none the same shape and none in a row, a little dimmer and a little green, which is what old mirror glass gives back. Nothing in here is lit warm: the stove is shut, and nobody lights a lamp. If the browns ever go amber, this has become The Den.
_thirteen: Thirteen stools, tables, windows, mirrors, columns and ceiling fans are Jim Butcher's numbers, from the books, and the tool counts them: a count that belongs to somebody else is a fact to protect, Swaying Sweetgrass's rule about its bundles. No two of any of them are alike and none of them stand in a row, because the books call the pub a study in deliberate asymmetry; the tool refuses two the same and refuses a row.
_inches: Every measurement in this file is in inches, because the standard the floor is built to is written in inches. The plan's origin is the north-west corner of the room: x runs east along the street wall, y runs south away from it, and z is height above the floor.
_source_of_the_brief: Ryan's brief linked the Dresden Files fan wiki's page for McAnally's. Nothing here is drawn from it: a fan wiki is a description of somebody's invented world written by other people, which is Sithen's reason for not using one. The room is built from the passages of the books Ryan quoted, read off his own Kindle copies, and every quotation names its book.

quotes.for: nothing in the pub to go haywire
quotes.words: There aren’t any video games at McAnally’s. There are no televisions or expensive computer trivia games. There isn’t even a jukebox. Mac keeps a player piano instead. It’s less likely to go haywire around us.

quotes.for: the steps and the fans, which this pub does differently
quotes.words: When you walk in, you take several steps down into a room with a deadly combination of a low clearance and ceiling fans.

quotes.for: fetching your order, which this pub does differently
quotes.words: And you can damn well walk your own self over to the bar to pick up your order when it’s ready, according to Mac.

quotes.for: what it is like to walk in
quotes.words: The first time I entered McAnally’s, I felt like a wolf returning to an old, favorite den.
There’s a sign Mac’s got hanging up at the door that reads ACCORDED NEUTRAL GROUND.

_quote_cap: Butcher's words are quoted to say what this room owes the books and where it parts from them, never to retell them. Forty words to a quotation fits his sentence about the machines and refuses a scene; a hundred and sixty in all is the drift guard, the Zibaldone's reason: nobody decides to republish a book, they add one good line at a time. Raise either number on purpose, here, with the reason written down, and never to fit one passage.
_books: Each Open Library work id was resolved on 2026-10-05 by searching Open Library for the title and Jim Butcher, then asking the work record itself, which names his author record (OL5152266A) on all four. None of them was typed from memory. The page numbers are Ryan Boren's Kindle edition's, as he quoted them, and the words were read off his quotation, not checked against a printed copy.

_rolls: THE PLAYER PIANO'S ROLLS. Each is a recording of a real piano roll, on its own page on Wikimedia Commons, where it is public domain, and the pub streams the MP3 Commons makes of it: nothing musical is hosted here, and nothing is fetched until somebody presses a roll. A roll is a strip, not a screen, so the pub's homage holds: nothing behind the bar has a screen. Every roll was chosen on 2026-10-06 from Commons' own descriptions, which say which roll it is and what it was played on; files that turned out to be notation software playing sheet music rather than a roll were left off. Every composer died more than seventy years ago, checked on Wikipedia against this year, so the music is public domain everywhere and not only in the United States, the Doomscroll's bar; that left off several rolls of songs whose writers died too recently, and one whose lyricist's dates could not be found. Every runtime was measured off the MP3 with ffprobe. How each recording was made is said only where its Commons page says it, and left out where it does not.
